_comment: NETWORKS WHOSE UPSTREAM IS GONE, so a repairable refusal on them is no longer repairable.
THIS IS NOT A CHANGE TO `refusal-reasons.json`, AND IT MUST NOT BECOME ONE. That file
classifies each MEMBER `permanent` or `repairable`, once, for every chain — and those
classifications are still right. `not-attempted` really does mean the run stopped rather
than the chain refusing, and on a chain whose network is still up, re-running the range
still produces the trace. Sui's `runtime-refused` rows are the live example: a Sui build
with trace hooks in pre-38 layers would trace them, so they are repairable and must keep
saying so.
What this file carries is the OTHER half of the claim, which no member can carry: whether
the network that would serve the repair still exists. Durability is a property of the
PAIR (member, chain), and splitting it this way is what keeps one chain's obituary from
rewording another chain's rows.
A CHAIN LISTED HERE DOES NOT LOSE ITS PUBLISHED REASONS. Every row keeps the member and
the sentence the producer wrote, because both were TRUE WHEN WRITTEN — the repair really
was available then. What changes is only the durability the page infers from them, which
is the one claim that silently went stale when the network went away.
EVIDENCE IS REQUIRED AND IS A MEASUREMENT, not a press release. The test is not whether
the endpoint answers — a restarted rollup answers perfectly well, at its own low block
numbers, and a request for a LOW height even returns a plausible header belonging to a
different chain. The test is whether the endpoint still serves a height inside the range
we captured.
WHY `aztec` AND `aztec-testnet` ARE NO LONGER LISTED (2026-11-26). Not because those
rollups came back -- they are gone and stay gone. The two SLUGS were handed to their
successors: the live rollups `tools/chain/follow-to-tip.mjs` tracks, published under the
plain names by the operator's decision for the first production corpus.
THIS FILE IS KEYED ON THE SLUG AND HAS NO ROOM FOR TWO DEPLOYMENTS UNDER ONE NAME. It is
read at twelve render sites through `isRetiredNetwork(chain)`, which is handed a slug and
nothing else. A slug left here while the follower publishes fresh rows under it would word
EVERY new row `akStranded` -- "no trace was recorded for this execution, and none can be
now" -- on a transaction whose chain is up, whose range is replayable and whose repair is
one dispatch away. That is a worse claim than the one this file exists to prevent, and it
would land on the whole production corpus instead of a frozen one. The frozen corpora at
the old deployments are discarded rather than republished, which is what makes the removal
safe.
AND IT IS NOW GATED IN TWO PLACES, because nothing compared this file with anything until
the collision had already been made. `src/blocktracer/chain/retired_networks.nim` fails the
BUILD when a chain listed here also appears in `tools/chain/chain-identity.json` (the
forward-looking half: what we last verified we can decode, and against which deployment).
`tools/chain/follow-to-tip-selftest.mjs` compares this file against the follower's own
endpoint table, which is the list that names both live chains. Two languages, two lists,
because one list is one thing to forget.

networks.evidence: The same rollup as `aztec-testnet`, captured through the same endpoint for its Noir call frames, and retired with it.
networks.note: Aztec testnet was restarted after this history was captured. The network that served it no longer exists, so no transaction here can be re-executed, whatever an individual row's published reason says about what that run did or did not try.
